characteristics.cultivar: Yunnan var. assamica adapted to Guangdong climate

description.short: Rich southern black tea reminiscent of Assam, adorned with golden tips
description.overview: One of the few prominent black teas of southern China, developed in the mid-20th century specifically for mass export with an emphasis on strength and briskness characteristic of Indian teas.
description.leaf: Dark, medium-sized leaves intermixed with golden tips
description.liquor: Rich deep red liquor, reminiscent of Assam tea
description.aroma: Malty, gently sweet, with nuances of cocoa
description.taste: Bold, full-bodied, with a satisfyingly dense texture
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Developed in the 1950s as part of a national initiative to expand black tea exports, utilizing Yunnan large-leaf plant material adapted to the subtropical climate of Guangdong
history.development: Thanks to Guangdong's warmer and more humid climate compared to Yunnan, the cultivar yields an especially bold and robust tea resembling Assam in profile
history.modern: One of the few widely produced black teas of southern China initially oriented toward international export rather than domestic consumption
interestingFacts: Specially formulated to cater to Western (especially British) taste preferences that favored bold, milk-compatible teas similar to Indian varieties
Utilizes large-leaf var. assamica material introduced from Yunnan rather than indigenous southern Chinese varieties
